beats.narration: Marcus Tan's application lands in the Onboarding inbox: start a Caldova Pension with $1,250,000, paying $78,000 a year monthly, with Helen as reversionary beneficiary.
Olivia's agent extracts the commencement amount, income, payment frequency, reversionary nomination and bank details, then runs the NIGO checklist.
Olivia opens case REQ-20261109-OPS003 for new pension account CP-3077881 and routes it to Benefits & Eligibility.
Ben checks the condition of release, the transfer balance cap, the minimum drawdown and the reversionary nomination.
Ben confirms George is 66 — condition of release met; $1.25m is within the $2.1m transfer balance cap; $78,000 a year is above the pro-rated $38,870 minimum, and Helen can be reversionary.
Ivy builds the income strategy: a cash bucket of two years' payments ($156,000) in cash and term deposits, with the rest in the Balanced model — three strategies compared in a workbook.
Rory moves $1,250,000 from accumulation into the new pension account, leaving $34,600 in super, and lines up the transfer balance account report for the ATO.
Ben hands the case to Payments to commence the pension.
Penny raises a Microsoft Teams approval card (commencements of $1m or more need sign-off), then commences the pension on 16 Nov 2026 — first $6,500 payment on 15 Dec 2026.
Cara sends George a warm "welcome to retirement" letter — his pension payments are tax-free from age 60 — and confirms everything with Marcus Tan.

result.headline: Pension started — first payment 15 December
result.summary: Outcome: COMPLETED — $1,250,000 Caldova Pension commenced; $78,000 a year paid monthly, Helen as reversionary beneficiary
